Last weekend while at the park I was watching these two older guys trying to fly what seemed to me to be advanced kites much more involved than your ordinary kites and these guys couldn't keep them in the air for more than 30 seconds. After about 30 minutes a couple of kids show up with basic children kites and they got them to fly and maintain their altitude within 10 seconds lol. I don't have fly kites but it looks fun and I just wanted to share what I saw.
I have only flown cheap kites. What would you suggest for a beginning kite flyer?

Delta kites are fun and easy to fly in most winds, but if you wanted to have a more active flying experience id recommend a box kite like This (I have one of these and it is fun to watch it bob around in the wind) or This

Box kites are fun, however you need some good winds (5+ mph) to fly them well. Now getting back to the delta kites prism makes some nice stowaway kites. Delta kites will fly in most winds (3-12+mph) and with the larger ones you can actually fly different tails/streamers or other things from them.

I like flat and bowed. Easy to build, easy to decorate, fun and easy to fly, easy to transport and store. Not to say I don't like all the other styles too. I enjoy dual line flying (never could get the hang of four line tho). But the older I get the more and more I like just holding a one liner and playing tug with the wind.
Dual line flexifoil. Have a 3ft, 6ft, and 8ft. One time we stacked all three in decent wind and you needed a partner to help anchor you down.
